turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we'll be quick. Start with why Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, before anyone called me.
"Get this over with." I'm writing that down. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.
My son does not lie, and "everyone knows" is not a document. Show me what you have, or I'm in the principal's office before you've packed your bag.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.
I'm not here as a lawyer, Hale, I'm here as his mother. Your school's own procedure, 4.2, says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Explain that.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?
That's your choice, not mine. Answer 4.2, or I walk down the hall to the principal's office right now and we do this there.
